appraisal_events.evidence: Devant le remerciement « d'une ardeur réfrigérante », Norpois prend « une expression d'hésitation et de mécontentement » et suppose « quelque visée suspecte, quelque faute antérieure » ; « je compris que cette commission, il ne la ferait jamais ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's excessive gratitude backfires: Norpois silently withdraws the promised recommendation and privately reclassifies the boy as suspect, so the narrator is refused access to Mme Swann's house without a word being spoken.

appraisal_events.evidence: L'entrefilet parle d'« un triomphe comme elle en a rarement connu de plus éclatant au cours de sa prestigieuse carrière » et de « la plus pure et la plus haute manifestation d'art » ; le narrateur s'écrie alors : « Quelle grande artiste ! »
appraisal_events.explanation: The press and the "juges les plus autorisés" consecrate la Berma's Phèdre as a public triumph, and the narrator's own cry of admiration follows; the narrator immediately ironizes the mechanism by which this borrowed authority feeds his imperfect pleasure "en véritable parasite".

status_effects.explanation: He is definitively shut out of the Swann household: the commission will never be transmitted, and Odette will never learn that he exists or wishes to come.

His words produce the exact opposite of their intent — of all possible phrases they were "les seules qui pussent avoir pour résultat de l'y faire renoncer" — so his speech is staged as self-defeating.
Locally she is raised to the summit of contemporary art by authorized public judgment, a triumph the narrator then adopts as his own verdict.

ambiguities: The irony surrounding la Berma's consecration falls on the narrator's parasitic mechanism of admiration ("Sans doute on peut trouver que je n'étais pas absolument sincère"), not on the performance itself; the passage never disputes her merit, so her local elevation stands even though the enthusiasm reporting it is discredited.

Norpois could also be read as locally diminished, since the narration exposes his ungenerous suspicion and his silent breach of a promise; no separate event is emitted because the passage's dominant framing is the narrator's own misjudged effusion and the access he loses by it.
